paint.finish_family.description: Paint finish family (from Honda's name: Pearl = mica/pearlescent effect pigment)

candidates.notes: Only the word 'Pearl' is sourced. Number of coats (2-coat vs 3-coat tri-coat), pigment and flake type are not published; see paint.layer_structure.

paint.option_cost_us_2022.description: Sonic Gray paint was an extra-cost option on the C&D 2022 test car (identity cross-check only)

candidates.notes: Same test car: 'Our Sonic Gray Civic Sport Touring test car'. Photos of it are catalogued in references/manifest.json (not downloadable: robots.txt).

candidates.how_to_measure: Ask a Honda body shop / paint supplier (PPG, Axalta, BASF) for the NH-877P refinish formula: it states whether a mid-coat is needed. Measure a clean, polished body panel (door skin) of the real car with a multi-angle spectrophotometer (e.g. X-Rite MA-T12 / BYK-mac i: L*a*b* at 15/25/45/75/110 deg aspecular, sparkle and graininess) or at minimum photograph the panel beside an X-Rite ColorChecker in open shade, RAW, fixed white balance, at several viewing angles.

paint.clearcoat_ior.description: Clearcoat refractive index (for a layered BRDF)

candidates.how_to_measure: Not practical to measure on the car; accept the generic value or ask the refinish supplier for the clearcoat chemistry.
candidates.notes: Basis: OEM automotive clearcoats are acrylic/urethane polymers with refractive index about 1.45-1.55. Not specific to NH-877P.

paint.clearcoat_roughness.description: Clearcoat roughness (GGX perceptual roughness, new clean car)

candidates.how_to_measure: Measure 20-degree gloss (GU) on a cleaned panel with a glossmeter (OEM clearcoats are typically 85-95 GU at 20 deg) and map to roughness, or photograph a straight light reflection on the hood and fit the highlight width.
candidates.notes: Basis: factory clearcoat on a new car gives sharp, mirror-like reflections (press photos show sharp building reflections on the doors). Engineering judgement, not measured; orange peel is a separate low-frequency normal effect.

paint.base_roughness.description: Base/pearl layer roughness under the clearcoat (GGX perceptual)

candidates.how_to_measure: Measure a clean, polished body panel (door skin) of the real car with a multi-angle spectrophotometer (e.g. X-Rite MA-T12 / BYK-mac i: L*a*b* at 15/25/45/75/110 deg aspecular, sparkle and graininess) or at minimum photograph the panel beside an X-Rite ColorChecker in open shade, RAW, fixed white balance, at several viewing angles.
candidates.notes: Basis: effect-pigment base coats scatter broadly (soft pearl glow rather than a second sharp highlight). Judgement only.

paint.flake.description: Flake / effect pigment type, size and density

candidates.how_to_measure: Macro photograph (1:1, ring light, 45 deg) of a clean panel next to a mm scale to see flake size and density; or a sparkle/graininess reading from a BYK-mac i. Measure a clean, polished body panel (door skin) of the real car with a multi-angle spectrophotometer (e.g. X-Rite MA-T12 / BYK-mac i: L*a*b* at 15/25/45/75/110 deg aspecular, sparkle and graininess) or at minimum photograph the panel beside an X-Rite ColorChecker in open shade, RAW, fixed white balance, at several viewing angles.
candidates.notes: 'Pearl' implies mica-type (interference) pigment rather than aluminium metallic flake, but the mix is unpublished.
